title: Promise and Harbor
premise: Wren Montrose, a pastry chef drowning in café debt and a decade-old family wound, hires marina mechanic Theo Vasquez to pose as their partner at the Montrose family's coastal festival weekend. What begins as a transactional arrangement deepens as Theo sees through Wren's practiced invisibility, and Wren realizes the 'sentence' they've rehearsed for ten years—an apology to their estranged mother—is really about admitting they deserve to be seen. When the fake relationship is exposed at the festival's closing bonfire, Wren must choose between retreating into safety or speaking both truths: the apology and the love they never planned to feel. They end the festival having saved neither the performance nor the secret, but finally claiming a place—and a person—to belong to.
about_author: Xanthe Villalobos is a former line cook who traded kitchen heat for the quieter warmth of love stories set in small coastal towns. She writes about people who are better at feeding others than at feeding themselves.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A bank notice arrives the same morning Wren burns a batch of macarons—the first failure in years. Establishing beat: exhaustion masked as control, and the café as both dream and cage.

chapters.title: The Invitation with a Plus-One
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Montrose family reunion invitation arrives, and Wren drafts an excuse for the tenth year running—until the bank calls again and pride intervenes. Emotional beat: the cost of invisibility made concrete.

chapters.title: A Mechanic by the Water
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren meets Theo Vasquez fixing a charter boat near the marina and, on impulse over shared chowder, proposes the fake-date arrangement. Beat: reckless hope disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo agrees—for rent money and reasons he doesn't examine too closely. They negotiate rules: no real feelings, no real names of exes, no staying past Sunday. Beat: two guarded people building walls together.

chapters.title: Arrival at Saltcrest House
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The couple arrives at the family estate; Wren's mother greets them with polite frost, and Theo witnesses the wound firsthand. Beat: the performance begins, and it costs more than expected.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Wren takes over the reunion's dessert course, and watching them work, Theo forgets to act—he simply looks. A stolen moment in the pantry nearly breaks rule one. Beat: desire outrunning the contract.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Half-Spoken
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Cornered by their mother on the garden path, Wren almost says the rehearsed sentence but swallows it; Theo covers for them, and later Wren snaps at him for seeing too much. Beat: fear weaponized against intimacy.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Harbor
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm strands everyone indoors; power fails, and by candlelight Wren tells Theo the truth behind the decade of silence. Beat: vulnerability exchanged like contraband, feelings now undeniable.

chapters.title: Exposed at the Bonfire
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the closing bonfire, a cousin reveals the arrangement was bought and paid for; humiliated before the whole family, Wren flees to the harbor with Theo following. Climax: everything false collapses, forcing what's true to surface.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returns
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the dark dock, Wren finally speaks the sentence—not just the apology, but the admission of love—and Theo admits he stopped pretending days ago. Resolution: no neat rescue of the café, but a partnership, personal and possibly professional, worth building.
